_comment: Entry PURPOSE RESOLUTION for a synthetic / provider-error stub: (plan, hard fallback) -> the `request_purpose` the relay puts on the wire when an entry produced no upstream response. The rule is program.purpose, else requests[0].purpose, else the caller's hard fallback — with an EMPTY STRING treated as absent at both levels, because `request_purpose` is a required wire field and a blank one is not a value. No reference implementation: the rule above IS the contract, and every relay conforms to it. Consumers: entryPurposeOr (browser frontend/src/lib/refresh/orchestrator.ts), _entry_purpose + `or <fallback>` (CLI orchestrator.py), entryPurpose(_:fallback:) (macOS RefreshOrchestrator.swift). Every suite drives the FALLBACK-RESOLVED operation, not the raw derivation, because the resolved value is the one that reaches the wire. AUTHORED input, AUTHORED expect - this corpus is NOT regenerated by `make gen-vectors`: it was written to converge a browser that resolved this wrongly, so generating the expectations from the browser reference would have enshrined the defect as the contract. `make gen-vectors` still rewrites MANIFEST.sha256 and vendors this file into the two ports.

vectors.name: a program plan carries no requests[], so the program's purpose is the answer
a flat plan resolves to its first request's purpose
an empty program purpose falls through to the first request's, it does not stop at the empty string
the program's purpose wins over the first request's when both are present
an empty program purpose with no requests falls all the way to the hard fallback
a flat request whose purpose is empty takes the hard fallback, never the empty string
an empty requests[] with no program takes the hard fallback
a plan with neither key takes the hard fallback
